repos.code_reuse_terms: MIT: retain copyright notice in copies/substantial portions; patterns and prose freely reusable; soft academic-citation ask for the arXiv paper if the skill materially contributed to a manuscript
reusable_patterns: Seven-phase systematic review workflow: planning -> systematic search -> screening -> extraction/quality -> synthesis -> citation verification -> document generation

Decoupled search vs processing: live search done by agent/other scripts; search_databases.py is a pure offline pipeline over normalized JSON records (dedupe DOI-first, year filter, rank, summary, json/markdown/bibtex output) with no network calls
Explicit refusal of raw provider envelopes: input must be a normalized record array
Citation verification scoped honestly: DOI registration (doi.org handle API) + Crossref metadata only; statuses registered/missing/inconclusive/invalid_syntax; no claim-support or retraction checking
Bounded transient retries with Retry-After awareness; rate-limit awareness (<=2 req/s to Crossref)
BibTeX key scheme: first_author+year with numeric collision suffixes
Metadata enrichment as mandatory phase: treat API records as incomplete; never invent fields; distinguish missing vs not-applicable
Credential hygiene: each API key sent only to its own service, never bundled
risks: No claim-to-citation matching; DOI registration != citation support (their own pitfall #4)
Crossref coverage gaps -> inconclusive/metadata_unavailable buckets need manual review
DOI regex extraction is inherently ambiguous in prose
Skill is prose-driven: agent executes phases manually; scripts are narrow offline helpers, not an automated pipeline
Optional paid external dependencies (parallel-cli, OpenRouter) for discovery/schematics
PRISMA/systematic rigor depends on agent discipline, not code enforcement

repos.code_reuse_terms: Apache-2.0 permissive: may copy code if license/copyright retained, changes stated, license distributed; includes patent grant; ideas/patterns freely reusable; no NOTICE obligations
reusable_patterns: Four-stage agent pipeline: OutlineAgent (plan -> outline.json) -> HybridLiteratureAgent (discovery+synthesis) -> SectionWritingAgent (body) -> ContentRefinementAgent (critique, <=3 reflection rounds + VLM format review)

Planning artifact as typed JSON outline: intro_related_work_plan (search_directions, subsection limitation_search_queries) + section_plan blueprint with citation_hints; discovery tasks are mechanically derived from the plan (_collect_search_tasks)
Hybrid discovery: parallel LLM+Google-Search candidate discovery (10-thread pool), then sequential rate-limited Semantic Scholar enrichment with cutoff filtering and title normalization dedup
Typed Pydantic intermediates: CandidatePaper, DiscoveryResult (injected into prompts via model_json_schema()), PaperData (enriched record), WriterOutput
citation_map.json: key->(title/authors/venue/year/abstract) lookup consumed by section writers; bibtex generated from the same registry
Citation coverage hard rule in synthesis: min_cite_paper_count = 90% of collected papers
Coarse batch-level resume: paper_writing_log.json records per-paper success for skipping completed work in batch runs
Whole-pipeline retry loop (max 3 tries) around the agent chain
risks: API key printed in plaintext at import: utils/scholar_utils.py line 28 `print(f"Using S2 API Key: {S2_API_KEY}")` — must NOT copy
Task tracking is in-memory only (per-process registry + processed-task set; nothing persisted); crash loses all discovery progress — confirmed in HybridLiteratureAgent.run()
Provider-locked: hard-coded Gemini model defaults (gemini-3.1-pro-preview / gemini-3-flash-preview)
Silent degradation: discovery retries 3x then returns empty candidates; enrichment exceptions swallowed with bare `except: pass`
Fuzzy title matching threshold >70 with year-hint +10 bias can select the wrong record
Abstracts truncated to 1500 chars — synthesis context loss
No feedback from critique back into planning; critique failure only triggers full pipeline restart
Cutoff-date filtering logic duplicated in agent and scholar_utils with divergent semantics
Sequential 1s sleep between Semantic Scholar queries is slow for large candidate sets
